questions.prompt: What are the three things you do in the first 15 minutes of a shift?
questions.modelAnswer: Read the handover notes, check today's arrivals, and walk the lobby.

questions.prompt: Name two of the key standards from the Role Overview that involve a specific number.
questions.modelAnswer: Greet every guest within 10 seconds; never promise compensation over $50 without Duty Manager approval; nothing sits unassigned on the task board for more than 15 minutes.
keyPoints: Compensation over $50 needs Duty Manager approval

questions.prompt: Someone calls saying they are a guest's spouse and asks for the room number. What do you do and why?
questions.modelAnswer: Do not confirm whether the person is a guest or give out the room number — only the registered guest gets that information. Direct the caller to the Duty Manager.
keyPoints: Never confirm a room number to anyone but the registered guest
Direct them to the Duty Manager

questions.prompt: Describe the phone standards: rings, hold, and what you do before ending a call.
questions.modelAnswer: Answer within three rings, ask permission before placing a guest on hold and check back within 60 seconds, and repeat back any request or reservation detail before ending the call.
keyPoints: Check back on hold within 60 seconds
Repeat back the request before ending

questions.modelAnswer: Make eye contact and smile when a guest is 10 feet away, and greet them verbally at 5 feet.
keyPoints: Eye contact and smile at 10 feet
